tests.question: Do primary arguments on incomplete social orderings, population ethics, person-affecting reasons, and interpersonal welfare comparison already make this distinction or a stronger version?
actions: Retrieve and read targeted primary passages on completeness/incompleteness in social choice and welfare comparison.
Retrieve and read the closest primary arguments about comparing persons' lives or benefits in population ethics.
Retrieve and read primary distributive arguments on priority, prior access, and lifetime disadvantage.
Record exact editions, URLs, queries, retrieved bytes, read spans, and unavailable items; compare the argument's actual inferential steps rather than its title or vocabulary.

tests.outcome_if-familiar: Withdraw any originality suggestion; isolate a narrower diagnostic only if the sources leave it defensible, otherwise set aside.

tests.question: Can a specified claim-priority rule guide connected finite decisions without cycles or dependence on irrelevant whole-life details?
actions: Define a finite set of patients, interventions, relevant context variables, and a transparent edge-generation rule.
Enumerate the graph for every menu under a fixed context; search for strict cycles and verify maximal options.
Change only details declared irrelevant and check that edge directions are invariant.
Change relevant baseline disadvantage or prior allocation and record which changes in priority the rule permits and why.
Compare at least two distinct complete extensions of any incomplete relation to check whether they reverse a whole-life comparison while preserving all local edges.
tests.failure_condition: Any same-context cycle, unexplained menu reversal, or inability to state the relevant context defeats the proposed procedure.

tests.question: Can the severity/corrective-priority example be defended, and can incomparable maxima be handled without hiding a whole-life ranking?
actions: Construct a serious rival rule that prioritizes a different defensible claim.
Test repeated decisions with updated allocation histories and protected rights.
Defend a fair lottery or another neutral tie procedure independently; if none is defensible, retain underdetermination.
tests.failure_condition: If relevant distributive claims require complete-life aggregation, narrow or reject the central claim.
